name_reason: Already fully compliant: data_fd2_ prefix, battle core-table qualifier (_battle_), descriptor reflects both the data shape (table) and semantics (y_offset). '10color' is a meaningful domain dimension (10 color phases of the variant-A summon-spell animation), 'variant_a' distinguishes it from the identical-valued variant_b sibling table @ 0x524D0. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Read-only per-color vertical (Y) pixel-offset table for the 10 color phases of the variant-A summon-spell (zhao-huan) 6-slot animation.
logic_summary: Sole consumer fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot (@ 0x269D3) copies the whole table to a stack-local int[10] (MOV ECX,0xA / MOV ESI,0x524A8 / REP MOVSD). If the casting unit is on the enemy team (runtime_char[caster].bTeam == 0) every local entry is biased by +0x8F. During tick states {2,5,8} each animated slot's screen y is origin_y + local_offset[color_idx], where color_idx is the per-slot rotating color index (0..9). The bias and indexing all operate on the consumer's local copy, so the global is never written.
element_semantics: Each element is the vertical (Y) row pixel offset for one of the 10 color phases of the variant-A summon animation. Values (LE) = {30,50,70,40,80,100,70,30,60,90}.
comment_original_issue: The pre-existing src comment was accurate but omitted the enemy-team +0x8F bias that the consumer applies to its local copy, and did not mention the whole-table REP MOVSD copy. Sibling table comments in the same file (e.g. the 12-slot table notes '+0x14 for the enemy team') do call out their team adjustment, so the variant-A comment was less complete/consistent than its siblings.
notes: Only xrefs to 0x524A8 are the DATA address-load (0x269ED) and READ (0x269F2) inside fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot; no writers, confirming is_const=true (declaration already const). Memory readback (40 bytes = 10 u32) and disassembly (MOV ECX,0xA + REP MOVSD) confirm int32[10]. Ghidra data plate at 0x524A8 was null (no function -> get_plate_comment 'No function' was expected); created a PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline. The 'failing scripts' noise in run_script_inline output is stale cached scripts in the user's ghidra_scripts dir, unrelated to this run; my scripts reported PLATE_START/PLATE_SET_OK and ran to completion.
